description: Baseline eval fixture for PP-004: how long it takes this second reference app to prove itself from a torn-down, clean-environment starting state, and what evidence backs each R0-R3 control. Comparable to evidence/../../nextjs-postgres-crud/evidence/pp-003-eval-fixture.json — same task-board domain, same profile, a materially different stack (React/Vite SPA + FastAPI + SQLAlchemy/Alembic instead of Next.js + Prisma).

stack.capabilityPack: none — no capability pack exists yet for this stack; auth/RBAC is built directly into backend/app (see docs/runbook.md)

cleanEnvironmentRehearsal.scope: docker compose down -v, fresh Postgres, alembic upgrade head, seed, docker build --no-cache, run, health check, smoke test, teardown

migrationRollbackRehearsal.scope: verify schema, alembic downgrade base, verify dropped, alembic upgrade head + seed, verify restored

readinessCheck.result: PENDING at the time this fixture was generated — every control except ci already has real, checked evidence locally (pytest, ruff, mypy, npm typecheck/lint/build, Playwright e2e incl. accessibility and performance, a real Alembic upgrade/downgrade/upgrade rehearsal, a real docker build + clean-environment rehearsal, and clean pip-audit/npm audit/gitleaks scans). ci stays pending until a real GitHub Actions run completes after pushing (see docs/requirements-traceability.md's 'Not yet closed' section and development/state.json's lastSession for the current status). One genuine finding along the way: pip-audit's initial run against the pinned lockfile found 7 known advisories in a transitively-pinned starlette version pulled in by fastapi's loose >=0.46.0 bound; fixed by pinning starlette directly (see docs/security-notes.md), not documented-and-ignored.
